title: Toolcall compatibility hysteresis and probation rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a probabilistic, hysteresis-driven compatibility checker for tool-calling (function signatures / structured output) to be used during canary and A/B rollouts. The goal is to detect semantically incompatible changes in function-call shapes and structured outputs early, reduce false positives with a probation window, and enable automated, safe partial rollbacks when a compatibility regression is both statistically significant and operationally meaningful.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility scorer runs for every canary invocation and produces a numeric incompatibility score
Probation window (configurable, default 1 hour) avoids immediate auto-unwinding for transient spikes
Hysteresis thresholds are implemented: soft threshold triggers alerts and increased sampling; hard threshold triggers automated partial rollback according to policy
Telemetry dashboard with per-variant signature-delta rates, latency delta, and downstream error rate is available
E2E tests covering: exact signature additions/removals, arg-type widening/narrowing, missing required fields in structured output, and extraneous unexpected fields
Playbook document (links below) for manual override and postmortem is published and referenced by the rollback task
design_decisions: Use a delta-based compatibility score instead of binary pass/fail to account for benign additions (extra optional fields) vs breaking removals
Combine static schema diffs (from schema registry) with runtime evidence (frequency of offending invocations) to weight decisions
Probation period implements exponential backoff: repeated violations shorten probation for subsequent checks within a short window
Separate action paths: alert escalation, traffic quarantine (route small percent to canary-only path), and auto-partial-unwind when hard thresholds met
Default soft threshold = 0.02 (2% of calls show incompatible delta); hard threshold = 0.10 (10%) with at least N=1000 invocations in the sampling window
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to emit function-call shape signatures and structured output JSON schema hash per response
2) Build a lightweight compatibility scorer service that consumes runtime telemetry and the schema-registry diffs
3) Implement a probation/hysteresis state machine in rollout controller: state=OK -> SOFT_ALERT -> PROBATION -> HARD_ALERT -> UNWIND
4) Wire scorer decisions to the rollout controller with safe-mode options (dry-run, alert-only, partial-quarantine, auto-unwind)
5) Add new metrics to console: signature_delta_rate, probation_state_distribution, unwinds_triggered, avg_time_in_probation
6) Create unit/integration tests and a shadow traffic job to validate scorer behavior before enabling auto-unwind
risk_and_mitigation: False positives could cause unnecessary rollbacks: mitigate via probation + minimum invocation count and manual review hook
High-cardinality schemas may produce noisy diffs: mitigate by normalizing transient fields (timestamps, uuids) and whitelisting known non-deterministic keys
Latency overhead from telemetry: use sampling (default 2%) for high-volume routes and allow per-route overrides
Edge cases where schema changes are backward compatible but semantic regressions are not: link with quality-eval signals (BLEU/QA metrics) to augment scoring
test_plan: Create synthetic workloads that exercise: missing required arg, renamed keys, added enum values, changed arg types (string->int)
Run A/B experiment with 10% traffic and shadow full traffic to scorer; compare predicted incompatibility vs manually labeled ground truth
Inject transient noise (spike of 5% incompatible responses for 10 minutes) to ensure probation avoids spuriously unwinding
Chaos test: simulate scorer outage and verify rollout controller fails open (no automatic unwinds) and emits alerts
milestones: M2: compatibility scorer prototype deployed to staging (2026-03-18)
M3: rollout controller hysteresis state machine + console metrics (2026-03-22)
M4: GA with auto-unwind opt-in for select customers (2026-03-25)
